The Associate Registrar, Systems manages multiple functions and provides primary leadership, management, planning and coordination for all systems development with the Office of the Registrar. Develops short- and long-term departmental goals. Serves as key member of the Office of the Registrar Leadership Team and, in the absence of the University Registrar, provides departmental and operational authority with other members of the Leadership Team.

Under the direction of the University Registrar, the Associate Registrar, Systems is responsible for coordinating the overall delivery of student records functionality in the Peoplesoft Campus Solutions Academic Information System (AIS) and serves as a primary liaison and subject matter expert representing the Office of the Registrar to campuswide academic and administrative departments, including Information Technology Services (ITS) staff supporting AIS. As a member of the Registrar Systems team (Regsys) the incumbent acts as a technical and functional lead and mentor, and is responsible for accurate, efficient and timely delivery of systems to support the work of the department and the goals of the institution.

Aided by knowledge of industry best practices, this analyst interprets and ensures the implementation of complex policies and procedures, and works collaboratively with other Regsys analysts to maximize the efficiency and effectiveness of student records functionality and reporting. They regularly and within time constraints perform analysis, troubleshooting, and problem resolution across the full range of student records data, encompassing term activation, program/plan creation, enrollment, residency and tuition calculation, grading, student academic history, degree audit, transcripts, and evaluations. The incumbent will work closely with other Registrar analysts and managers (Curriculum, Advising, Scheduling, Degree Audit, Residency, VA Certification, Tuition & Fees) to implement enhancements, troubleshoot issues, and verify the accuracy and continuity of system integrations.

Areas of system development also include complex and time-sensitive ad hoc reporting and data mining using SQL; corporate enrollment and degree reporting to UCSC Budget Analysis and Planning and UC Office of the President; specification and maintenance of numerous student records interfaces to other campus offices and external entities; and the identification and implementation of changes to move from labor-intensive to streamlined self-service.
